title: TraceBalloon orchestration proposal and CI smoke harness
summary: Proposal for a lightweight dynamic tracing controller (TraceBalloon) and a companion CI smoke harness to capture targeted traces, produce flamegraphs, and validate profiling pipelines end-to-end in perf CI.
body:
Goal and motivation:

- Problem: intermittent tail-latency spikes and headroom regressions show up in production, but reproducing and collecting aligned stack traces across processes/GPUs is expensive and fragile. Existing samplers either create too much overhead or require intrusive agent changes.
- Goal: provide a minimal orchestration piece that can attach short-lived, low-overhead captures across a replica set, centralize artifacts, and produce consumable flamegraphs/trace bundles suitable for CI gating and postmortem.
- Constraints: must be safe for staging with realistic loads, cheap enough to run in CI smoke windows, and produce consistent artifacts (flamegraphs + trace metadata) that the perf team and oncall can interpret quickly.

Concept: TraceBalloon (short summary)

- TraceBalloon = small controller + per-node balloon agent. Controller triggers coordinated captures across a set of targets, each agent performs one of: user-space stackwalk sampling, light eBPF probes for IRQ/preempt events (configurable), and GPU device-side sample markers (when supported).
- Captures are intentionally short (configurable 5-30s) and adaptive: start low-sample-rate then burst on detected long tails.
- Output: compressed trace bundle (.tar.gz) containing raw perf.data (or eBPF JSON), resolved symbols, mapping metadata (git sha, model version, kernel info), and a generated flamegraph.svg.

Architecture and components:

- balloon-controller (go service, ephemeral job)
  - accepts capture spec: targets (label selectors), duration, sampler profile, trigger policy (immediate | tail-detection | scheduled), artifact destination
  - coordinates zookeeper-like barrier so captures across replicas are time-aligned within +/- 50ms
  - uploads artifacts to perf-s3 with standardized naming: service-env-model-YYYYMMDDTHHMM-uuid.tar.gz

- balloon-agent (rust small binary)
  - runs as a sidecar or host daemon; minimal surface area (no long running telemetry by default)
  - sampling modes: user-space stackwalk (perf_event), uprobe lite, eBPF histograms (counts), and GLTrace for GPU markers (where supported)
  - low-overhead default profile: sample every 2ms for first 5s (warmup), switch to burst 500us when tail-latency > threshold

- perf-ci-harness (github actions / k8s job)
  - small smoke pipeline step that invokes balloon-controller against the canary cluster after a PR lands to serving-runtime or perf infra changes
  - validates: artifact upload success, flamegraph generation, generated flamegraph size within expected bounds, and presence of top-N stack frames across traces (sanity check for symbolization)

CI smoke job workflow (high-level)

1. Post-merge or per-night PR: trigger perf-ci/traceballoon-smoke workflow (runs in staging environment with canary traffic).
2. Run synthetic workload: short-burst-long-tail microbench (we already have this workload as bench-suite/burst-tail) for 90s.
3. Invoke balloon-controller with trigger policy=scheduled, duration=20s, profile=default.
4. Wait for artifacts, run flamegraph generator (flamegraph.pl adapted for perf.data or eBPF traces).
5. Run smoke assertions: 
   - artifact present and checksums match
   - at least one trace contains symbolized frames for rust std and runtime hotpaths (serve::handle_request, kvcache::lookup, kernel entries if eBPF enabled)
   - top-3 hot functions aggregated token-percent do not exceed a regression threshold vs baseline (baseline stored in perf-metrics DB).
6. If CI asserts fail, attach artifact to PR and create JIRA stub (automated) linking PR and trace artifact.

Flamegraph generation and normalization rules:

- Standardize symbolization environment: use the same dockerized symbolizer image used by perf-team (link in linked_artifacts).
- Normalize timestamps to capture window; collapse short frames (<200us) to reduce noise.
- Add annotations on flamegraph top margin: sample count, profile id, commit sha, model id, node type, kernel version.

Collector and artifact retention policy:

- CI artifacts: keep for 90 days, tagged by PR/CI job id.
- Staging/Prod captures: keep for 14 days unless flagged for incident postmortem (manual flag extends to 1 year).
- Sensitive data: trace artifacts are scrubbed of pathnames and env vars by default; KMS-encrypt uploads for prod captures.

Operational runbook (quick steps)

- Oncall use-case: trigger an immediate capture with policy=tail-detection for the impacted service, duration=30s, profile=deep. Attach generated artifact to incident timeline.
- Debugging locally: run balloon-agent as a sidecar, `./balloon-agent --profile local-quick` and `balloon-controller --targets localhost --duration 10s --dest localdir/`
- Troubleshooting failed symbolization: verify binary docker image used for symbolizer matches artifact's commit sha; if not, attach mapping via git-submodule metadata in trace bundle.

Smoke CI YAML (conceptual, not exact):

- name: traceballoon-smoke
  runs-on: runner-k8s
  steps:
    - run: deploy bench-suite to staging-canary
    - run: run bench-suite --mode short-burst-long-tail --duration 90s
    - run: balloon-controller capture --targets serving=canary --duration 20 --profile default --dest s3://perf-artifacts/ci/${{ github.run_id }}
    - run: perf-tools generate-flamegraph s3://perf-artifacts/ci/${{ github.run_id }}/*.tar.gz --out flame.svg
    - run: perf-tools assert-flamegraph --baseline-id nightly-2025-01-01 --tolerance 5%

Security and safety checklist:

- Ensure agents run with minimal privileges; only perf_event and CAP_BPF when strictly necessary.
- Default CI runs must use staging clusters, not prod. Prod captures require a signed approver flow and KMS encryption.
- Add rate/usage limits: CI capture quota per repo per day to avoid cost blowups.

Open questions / TODOs:

- GPU capture story: current plan uses user-space marker injection + host-side alignment; need to validate on A100 and on-prem GPUs (ask infra for test nodes).
- Tail-detection heuristics: what window and percentile should we use for switching to burst sampling (P95? P99?). A/B test two policies in canary.
- Integration with observability console: propose a lightweight trace viewer card that links the flamegraph + raw bundle; ask product for mockups.
- Cost model: estimate additional S3 + CI runner minutes for nightly runs. Need finance roughs.

Appendix: Quick commands

- trigger local capture: `balloon-controller capture --targets local --duration 10 --profile local-quick --dest ./out/`
- list artifacts: `aws s3 ls s3://perf-artifacts/ci/ | grep traceballoon`
- generate flamegraph locally: `perf-tools generate-flamegraph ./out/*.tar.gz --out ./out/flame.svg`

Notes to reviewers:

- This is a working proposal; the goal is to get a minimal end-to-end CI smoke pipeline that produces human-readable flamegraphs and a deterministic artifact naming/retention scheme. Feedback requested on safety, CI gating thresholds, and whether to fold this into existing perf CI jobs or keep as separate workflow.

- If approved, next steps: small spike (2wk) to build balloon-agent prototype, end-to-end demo with canary, add perf CI smoke job, and then iterate on production safe guards.

Unresolved: exact baseline comparison metrics (define in follow-up PR).
